was: City of Worthington campground in Olson Park, near Lake Okabena, with bathhouses, a boat landing, the trail around the lake and a dog park: 58 sites with electric and 5 primitive ones, with water from central taps. --Claude
note: City of Worthington campground in Olson Park, on Sunset Bay of Lake Okabena, with bathhouses, a boat landing, the trail around the lake and a dog park.  Of its 58 sites with electric, sites 1-12 line the bay; there are also 5 primitive sites, and water comes from central taps. --Claude

was: Daiva RV Resorts park beside 2,500 ft of the Rocky Saugeen River, on more than 25 acres, over 19 of them left natural with walking trails.  The river drops 30 ft over a hydro-electric dam: upstream is deep enough for swimming, diving, boating and fishing, and downstream suits nature hikes and fly-fishing.  It has a heated pool, a playground and a comfort station, horseshoe pits, shuffleboard courts and badminton and volleyball nets, and planned activities such as Christmas in July, movie nights, children's crafts, horseshoe and euchre tournaments and dances.  It also has seasonal sites and a cabin. --Claude

was: Small family-owned campground on 42 acres of mostly natural forest in the Village of Warwick, Lambton County, with over 2 km of trails and a new dog park.  The camping area sits beside a 2-acre spring-fed lake, where motorized boats are not allowed, fishing is catch-and-release and there is no lifeguard.  Besides its powered sites it has off-grid sites, and each site takes one family with at most 2 adults and 2 pets.  Bottled drinking water and firewood are sold.  The name comes from the creek through the property, not from bears. --Claude

was: Campground at Havre Boucher with ocean-view RV sites and, in the E section, primitive sites beside the water.  Swimming is off the dock, in what the campground calls the warmest waters north of the Carolinas; there is no sandy beach, so water shoes are recommended, and there are canoes, kayaks and pedal boats.  There is beach-side volleyball, washer toss, a playground, a small walking trail, birdwatching (more than 30 kinds seen) and a book exchange.  Two cabins and a fifth-wheel trailer are rented, there are seasonal sites, and cyclists get a special rate for one tent.  Quiet hours run from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m. --Claude

was: Family resort on twenty-seven acres near Joplin, by Shoal Creek and a natural spring, with a restaurant on site.  Campers can fish in Shoal Creek and bring their own kayaks (there are no rentals, and self-shuttling costs $5 a car), and tent island, between the creek and the spring, is reached by footbridge.  Beach cabanas ($99 a night) and wagon lodging ($199) are rented, propane, wood and ice are sold, and a tank pump-out costs $10.  A day pass costs $5 a car, and a site may have two pets at most. --Claude
